newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb attack damages Corsican hairdressers.
newsitem.headline: Bomb attack damages Corsican hairdressers.

text.p: A bomb exploded outside a hairdressers shop in the Corsican town of Bastia overnight causing damage but no casualties, police said on Wednesday.
No one claimed responsibility for the attack which took place in the early hours when the shop was empty.
The attack bore the hallmarks of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC)-Historic Wing, which has stepped up a two-decade-old campaign for greater autonomy from France.
The FLNC traditionally carries out "punitive" actions against businesses which refuse to pay "revolutionary taxes" to finance its activities.
Francois Santoni, head of the Conculta Naziunalista, the FLNC's legal wing, is in prison in Paris facing charges for attempted extortion and bomb attacks.

The attack followed a statement by the FLNC in Ajaccio claiming responsibility for the placing of a large bomb outside a post office in Marseille on the French mainland on Saturday which was defused before exploding.
The statement also claimed responsibility for a bomb blast which damaged the entrance to the law courts in the Corsican town of Corte early on Tuesday. No one was hurt.
